skill.name: botsee
skill.description: Use the BotSee API to measure brand visibility, manage research inputs, inspect results, and generate visibility-focused content.
skill.summary: Run and manage BotSee AI visibility research from an agent workflow.
skill.author: rivalsee

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally contacts the BotSee API, persists local state, and writes generated content. Most high-severity static matches are false positives caused by API-key identifiers, documented config paths, UUID handling, and Markdown backticks. Two medium issues remain: sensitive files are permissioned after creation, and secrets can be passed through command-line arguments.

remediation.issue: Sensitive files can inherit permissive creation modes before chmod runs.
remediation.suggestion: Create ~/.botsee with mode 0700 first, then create temporary files with mode 0600 and atomically replace each target.

remediation.issue: Command-line flags accept API keys, tokens, and payment proofs.
remediation.suggestion: Accept secrets through protected environment variables, standard input, or a secure prompt, and discourage secret flags in documentation.

remediation.issue: BOTSEE_BASE_URL can redirect authenticated API requests.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the configured URL, require HTTPS, and require explicit confirmation before sending credentials to a non-BotSee host.

remediation.issue: Generated content uses a timestamped filename without exclusive creation.
remediation.suggestion: Check for an existing path or use exclusive creation before writing generated Markdown.

semantic_findings.title: Credential files created before restrictive permissions
semantic_findings.description: Two credential-writing paths apply mode 0600 only after writing. On a permissive or preexisting BotSee directory, another local user could briefly read signup tokens or API keys.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both functions visibly open and write sensitive files before calling chmod. The safer save_user_config path demonstrates that an umask can prevent this creation-time window.

semantic_findings.title: Secrets accepted through command-line arguments
semantic_findings.description: API keys, signup tokens, reset tokens, and payment proofs can be supplied as command arguments. These values may remain in shell history or appear in process listings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The argparse definitions and usage instructions explicitly place credential-like values after flags. Command arguments commonly persist outside the process receiving them.

content.user_title: Measure Brand Visibility Across AI Answers
content.value_statement: Brands struggle to measure how AI systems mention them and their competitors. BotSee manages research inputs, runs analyses, and turns results into actionable reports.
actual_capabilities: Create and manage sites, customer types, personas, and research questions through the BotSee API.
Run AI visibility analyses and poll until processing completes.
Display competitor, keyword, source, response, recommendation, and usage results.
Generate a blog post from the latest analysis and save it as Markdown.
Support credit-card signup, USDC signup, USDC top-ups, and account status checks.
Reset, rotate, revoke, store, and use BotSee API credentials.
limitations: A BotSee account, API access, network connectivity, and sufficient paid credits are required.
API credentials and pending signup state are stored under the user home directory.
Analysis can block for up to ten minutes and depends on BotSee service availability.
Generated content is written automatically to the current working directory.

use_cases.title: Track brand visibility
use_cases.description: Measure brand appearances, ranking, competitors, keywords, and cited sources across supported AI answer providers.

use_cases.title: Build audience research
use_cases.description: Create customer types, personas, and buyer questions before running a structured visibility analysis.

use_cases.title: Automate competitive reporting
use_cases.description: Run analyses, retrieve detailed results, inspect credit usage, and generate content from agent workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Check account status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my BotSee account status, active site, remaining credits, and available next actions. Do not start any paid operation.

prompt_templates.title: Set up a research site
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a BotSee site for [DOMAIN] with [TYPE_COUNT] customer types, [PERSONA_COUNT] personas per type, and [QUESTION_COUNT] questions per persona.

prompt_templates.title: Run and summarize analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a BotSee analysis for [SITE_UUID]. Summarize leading competitors, recurring keywords, cited sources, and remaining credits after completion.

prompt_templates.title: Compare detailed findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [SITE_UUID] using [MODELS] and [SCOPE]. Retrieve responses, competitors, keywords, sources, and recommendations, then identify three evidence-backed priorities.

output_examples.input: Check the active BotSee site and show the current account balance.
output_examples.output: Active site: Example Company. Remaining balance: 4,280 credits. No paid operation was started.

output_examples.input: Summarize the latest competitor results for the completed analysis.
output: Acme appears most often across the evaluated responses.
Northstar has the strongest average rank in the enterprise segment.
Three competitors account for most recorded mentions.

output_examples.input: Generate content from the latest analysis for the selected site.
output_examples.output: A blog post was generated from the latest analysis and saved as a timestamped Markdown file. The response also reports credits used.

best_practices: Check the active site and credit balance before starting analysis or generation.
Use explicit site and analysis identifiers when several projects are active.
Review generated content and recommendations before publishing or applying them.
anti_patterns: Do not place live API keys, reset tokens, or payment proofs in shared prompts or logs.
Do not retry create commands blindly because repeated calls can create duplicate resources.
Do not start paid analysis or generation without confirming the site, scope, and expected credit use.

faq.question: What does this skill measure?
faq.answer: It uses BotSee to measure brand mentions, competitors, rankings, keywords, sources, and AI responses.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill require a BotSee account?
faq.answer: Yes. Most operations require a BotSee API key, network access, and available credits.

faq.question: Where are credentials stored?
faq.answer: The skill stores the API key and active site in ~/.botsee/config.json.

faq.question: Does analysis finish immediately?
faq.answer: No. The command polls BotSee until completion and can wait for up to ten minutes.

faq.question: Does the skill write project files?
faq.answer: Yes. It writes workspace configuration and saves generated blog content as a timestamped Markdown file.
